result.summary: The image shows a signalized intersection with a marked crosswalk and basic sidewalk infrastructure. The pedestrian environment is characterized by wide travel lanes and degraded pavement conditions on the curb ramp, lacking dedicated pedestrian signals or traffic calming measures.

hazards.name: Degraded Curb and Sidewalk
hazards.description: The concrete at the curb ramp is significantly cracked and crumbling, creating a trip hazard and potential accessibility barrier.

hazards.name: Lack of Pedestrian Signals
hazards.description: No dedicated pedestrian signal heads are visible, forcing pedestrians to rely on vehicular signals which may not provide adequate clearance time.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Replace standard transverse markings with continental or ladder-style markings to increase visibility to drivers.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Countdown Signals
interventions.description: Install dedicated pedestrian signals with countdown timers to provide clear information on crossing time.

interventions.title: Curb Ramp Repair
interventions.description: Repair the crumbling concrete and ensure the ramp meets ADA standards with detectable warning surfaces.

result.summary: The intersection features marked zebra crosswalks and curb ramps with tactile warning pads, but the wide multi-lane roadway suggests a high-speed environment. While a wide grassy median provides some separation, the lack of visible pedestrian signals and the long crossing distance increase risk for non-motorized users.

hazards.name: Long Crossing Distance
hazards.description: Pedestrians must cross multiple lanes of traffic, increasing exposure time to vehicles.
hazards.location_in_image: Center foreground, the zebra crossing across the main road.

hazards.name: Lack of Pedestrian Signals
hazards.description: No dedicated pedestrian signal heads are visible at this signalized intersection, leaving pedestrians to rely on vehicle signals.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Countdown Signals
interventions.description: Install pedestrian signal heads with countdown timers to provide clear crossing intervals and improve safety at the signalized intersection.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk into the roadway at the crossing to shorten the crossing distance and improve visibility between drivers and pedestrians.

result.summary: The intersection features basic pedestrian infrastructure including high-visibility crosswalk markings, curb ramps, and a bus shelter. However, the environment is characterized by a wide roadway with multiple lanes and no median refuge, resulting in a long and exposed crossing distance for pedestrians.

hazards.name: Long crossing distance
hazards.description: The wide roadway lacks a median or refuge island, exposing pedestrians to traffic for an extended duration.
hazards.location_in_image: Center foreground across the main roadway

hazards.name: Degraded pavement
hazards.description: Visible cracking and wear on the asphalt surface can create tripping hazards or uneven footing.
hazards.location_in_image: Roadway surface in the foreground and intersection area

hazards.name: Lack of physical buffer
hazards.description: There is no vertical separation like trees or bollards between the sidewalk and the high-speed roadway.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side along the sidewalk edge

interventions.title: Pedestrian Refuge Island
interventions.description: Install a raised median island to provide a safe waiting area and allow for two-stage crossing.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Construct bulb-outs at the corners to shorten the crossing distance and increase pedestrian visibility.

interventions.title: Pavement Resurfacing
interventions.description: Repair and repave the intersection to provide a smooth, safe surface for all users.

result.summary: The environment is highly vehicle-oriented, featuring a wide multi-lane intersection with a complete absence of marked crosswalks or pedestrian signals. While a sidewalk and bus shelter are present, the lack of crossing infrastructure creates a hostile environment for pedestrians attempting to navigate the commercial corridor.
